skill.name: DevOps & Quality
skill.description: Guides teams on linting, formatting, version control, continuous integration, testing, and secrets management practices.
skill.summary: Apply practical DevOps and code-quality standards to a web project.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting and prose references. The skill contains guidance only; no executable code, secret access, network activity, or prompt-injection content was found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Rule**: strict type checking is enabled in `tsconfig.json`.
- **Commit Messages**: Semantic commits preferred (e.g., `feat: add chatbot`, `fix: header overflow`
- **GitHub Actions**: Recommended for running `npm run lint` and `npm run build` on every PR.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is Markdown documentation that names the npm run lint command inside inline code. It does not execute a command or accept input.
This line only references configuration filenames in Markdown. It contains no shell execution behavior.
This is a documentation reference to tsconfig.json, not a command invocation or executable code.
The inline text gives examples of semantic commit messages. It does not invoke a shell or execute commands.
The line recommends standard CI commands in prose only. No automation, command execution, or user-controlled input is present.
The .env reference is documentation about local secret storage. Backticks mark inline code and do not execute anything.
The skill advises that a local .env file must never be committed. It does not read, expose, or transmit environment-file contents.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent standards for quality checks and delivery workflows. This skill provides focused guidance for linting, testing, CI, and secret handling.
actual_capabilities: Recommends ESLint and strict TypeScript checking practices.
Suggests CI checks for linting and builds on pull requests.
Recommends Jest unit tests and Playwright end-to-end tests.
Explains local and production secret-management expectations.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not configure tools or workflows.
It does not generate CI workflow files or lint configurations.
It does not run tests, builds, or security scans.
Recommendations may require adaptation for the project stack.

use_cases.title: Set team quality standards
use_cases.description: Create a clear baseline for linting, type checking, commits, and tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare pull request checks
use_cases.description: Identify suitable lint and build checks for a continuous integration workflow.

use_cases.title: Review project practices
use_cases.description: Compare an existing web project against recommended quality and secret-handling practices.

prompt_templates.title: Start a quality checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevOps and Quality guidance to create a short checklist for my TypeScript project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan pull request checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on this skill, recommend lint, type-check, build, and test checks for every pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Review repository practices
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my project practices with this DevOps and Quality guidance. List gaps for branches, commits, tests, CI, and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Design an adoption plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased adoption plan for these quality standards. Include owners, pull request checks, testing priorities, and secret-management actions.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request quality checklist.
output: Run relevant Jest and Playwright tests.

output_examples.input: What should our CI workflow check?
output_examples.output: Run npm run lint and npm run build on every pull request. Add unit and end-to-end tests that match the changed areas.

best_practices: Run linting, type checks, builds, and relevant tests before merging.
Use feature branches and clear semantic commit messages.
Keep local secrets out of version control and use managed production variables.
anti_patterns: Do not commit .env files or production credentials.
Do not rely only on manual checks when CI can enforce standards.
Do not merge changes that fail linting, builds, or relevant tests.

faq.question: Does this skill run linting commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and does not execute commands.

faq.question: Which linter does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends ESLint for linting and formatting checks.

faq.question: Does it create GitHub Actions workflows?
faq.answer: No. It recommends CI checks but does not create workflow files.

faq.question: Which testing tools are mentioned?
faq.answer: It mentions Jest for unit tests and Playwright for end-to-end tests.

faq.question: How should local secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Keep them in a local .env file and never commit that file.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It offers process guidance and does not perform a security assessment.
